;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2011 Libyan civil war]]: After a lengthy and  bloody siege, [[National Transitional Council]] forces approach the center of the city of [[Sirte]], facing heavy resistance from troops loyal to the ousted dictator [[Muammar Gaddafi]]. [http://www.channel4.com/news/ferocious-fighting-in-sirte-as-ntc-tightens-grip (Channel 4 News)]
*Rocket fire and gunshots are reported in the [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] city of [[Kandahar]]. [http://news.xinhuanet.com/english2010/world/2011-10/09/c_131179980.htm (Xinhua)]

;International relations
*The [[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees]] opens a new [[refugee camp]] in western [[Ethiopia]] for refugees from [[Sudan]] and [[South Sudan]]. [https://web.archive.org/web/20111010032858/http://wireupdate.com/news/un-opens-new-camp-in-ethiopia-for-sudanese-refugees.html (BNO News)]

;Law and crime
*[[Law enforcement in Indonesia|Indonesian police]] arrest four people in connection with the [[suicide bombing]] of a [[mosque]] in [[Cirebon]], [[West Java]]. [http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2011/10/08/at-least-4-nabbed-cirebon-bombing-links.html (''Jakarta Post'')]

;Sport
*In [[horse racing]], the [[Australia]]n mare [[Black Caviar (horse)|Black Caviar]] ties the record set by [[Phar Lap]] for consecutive victories, with an unbeaten run of 14 wins. [http://www.abc.net.au/news/2011-10-08/black-caviar-returns-in-winning-style/3383950 (ABC News Australia)]

*In [[rugby league]], [[Leeds Rhinos]] win the [[2011_Super_League_Grand_Final|European Super League Grand Final]] at [[Old Trafford]] by defeating [[St_Helens_RLFC|St Helens]] 32-16. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/rugby_league/9606230.stm (BBC)]

;Transportation
*Stages 4 and 5 of [[Circle MRT line]] began operations, with all 12 stations along the Stage 4 and 5 of the MRT line from [[Caldecott MRT station|Caldecott]] to [[HarbourFront MRT station|HarbourFront]] (except [[Bukit Brown MRT station|Bukit Brown]]) being opened at the same time operated by [[SMRT Trains|SMRT Trains Ltd]].
